title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
abstract: arXiv:2611.06808v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Financial backtests of large language models (LLMs) are meaningful only if the model did not already know the outcomes it is asked to predict. Practitioners guard against this by trusting a vendor's stated knowledge cutoff, by asking the model what it knows, or by instructing it to answer as of a past date. To verify whether any of these safeguards can be trusted, we introduce FinDendro, a benchmark of 2,226 dated U.S. facts from 1999 to 2026, covering monthly macroeconomic series, month-end stock prices and Federal Reserve decisions. Each fact yields four prompts: a value question, Recall and Predict questions that pair each candidate value with a claim of knowing or guessing without a declared date, and a Predict question with a historical declared date. Controls for persistence and dominant outcomes keep chance accuracy near 0.27. Results show that for most frontier models, self-reports understate knowledge. GPT-5 answers 76% of contr

translated_title: 大语言模型不知道自己知道什么：面向金融回测的时间性自我知识基准测试
translated_abstract: 对大语言模型（LLM）进行金融回测只有在模型事先并不知晓其被要求预测的结果时才有意义。从业者通常通过信任供应商声明的知识截止日期、直接询问模型自己知道什么，或指示模型以过去某个日期为基准来回答，以此防范这一问题。为了验证这些保障措施是否可信，我们提出了FinDendro，一个包含1999年至2026年间2,226条带日期的美国事实的基准，涵盖月度宏观经济数据序列、月末股票价格和美联储决策。每个事实产生四个提示：一个数值提问、成对出现的Recall（回忆）与Predict（预测）问题——将每个候选数值与“知道”或“猜测”的声明配对但不声明日期——以及一个带有历史声明日期的Predict问题。针对结果持续性和主导性的对照设计使随机猜测的准确率保持在接近0.27的水平。结果表明，对大多数前沿模型而言，自我报告低估了其实际知识。GPT-5在回答76%的相关问题时……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 论文提出FinDendro基准（涵盖2,226条带日期的美国金融与宏观事实），发现大语言模型的自我报告会低估其实际知识，因此依赖知识截止日期声明或模型自述来确保金融回测有效性的做法并不可靠。
